page.layout: One printed page, single column of text. Top: woodcut ornament band. Below it the title block (centred headings). Then the salutation and the body paragraph with a large woodcut initial. Bottom centre: signature mark "* 2". No margin notes.

main_text.head: ILLUSTRIBUS ET PRÆPOTENTIBUS FRISIÆ ORDINIBUS
main_text.p: Nobilissimi, Amplissimi & Magnificentissimi Viri, ἀδελφοί admodum honorandi,

LIbellum hunc vobis inscribendum & dedicandum putavi, partim ut qualecunque grati animi ederem testimonium, partim ut eum florentissimæ Vestræ juventuti non parum profuturum, Frisiacis inquam paedagogeis, seu Scholis, ut loquuntur, trivialibus, commendaretis. Quod si

page.notes: The opening word "LIbellum" has a large woodcut initial I; the first letter is rendered as "L" with the initial "I" as printed ("Libellum"). The Greek word after "Viri," is partly illegible and was read as "ἀδελφοί" [?]; the printed form appears to be a Greek word for "brothers" (ἀδελφοῖς) in italic. The text "Frisiacis" and "paedagogeis" are italic Greek-Latin mixtures; "paedagogeis" appears as "paedagogeis" [?]. The title line "PRÆPOTENTIBUS" and "ILLUSTRIBUS ET" are in spaced capitals. Transcription of italic and roman mixed lines is approximate where letters are worn.
